figures.label: S1
figures.caption: Fig. S1 Statistical correlation between initial interfacial resistance (Rint) and CCD. Scatter plots and Spearman correlation analyses are presented for a) the entire aggregated dataset, revealing a general inverse trend. b) The subset of cells without interlayers, highlighting bare interfaces consistently fail at low CCDs due to high initial resistances. c) The subset of cells with Li-alloying interlayers. In this low-resistance regime, the negative correlation (R) is significantly weakened with an increased P-value, demonstrating that the direct relationship between initial contact quality and dynamic cycling stability breaks down.

figures.label: S11
figures.caption: Fig. S11 Temperature-dependent EIS spectra and Kramers-Kronig (K-K) validity test. Top panels present Nyquist plots with annotated frequency ranges and key frequency markers for LLZO electrolyte (brown), interfacial (yellow), and Li metal (gray) contributions, collected at specific temperatures: a) –20 °C, b) 0 °C, and c) 20 °C. The high-frequency response shifts into the measurable window at lower temperatures. Bottom panels show corresponding K-K residual plots for real (red) and imaginary (blue) components against frequency, assessing data quality suitable for further analysis.

figures.label: S12
figures.caption: Fig. S12 DRT analysis and equivalent circuit fitting validation. Three columns display results at distinct temperatures: a) –20 °C, b) 0 °C, and c) 20 °C. Top panels show experimental Nyquist data (circles) with overlaid 3-RQ equivalent circuit fits (solid lines), indicating apex frequencies marked for bulk (Bulk), grain-boundary (GB), and Li|LLZO interface (int) transport processes. Middle panels present DRT spectra derived using the regularization parameter of 0.005 and full-width-half-maximum (FWHM) of 0.5. Distinct peaks are assigned to specific physical contributions. The tables at the bottom summarize the fitted capacitance (C), resistance (R), relaxation time (τ), and characteristic frequency (f) for each deconvoluted component, demonstrating cross-validation between methods. The extreme low-frequency tail was excluded from the DRT and EIS fitting.
